content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of each type
Understand when each type is used
Apply knowledge to different contexts and organisms

Both aerobic and anaerobic respiration release energy from glucose, but they differ in their requirements, products, and efficiency. Understanding these differences helps explain how organisms cope with varying oxygen availability.
We always use one type or the other
Both types often occur simultaneously in different proportions
Each has advantages for different situations
All athletes use both types depending on the activity
Yeast and humans have the same anaerobic products
Yeast produces ethanol; humans produce lactic acid
Organism that cannot survive with oxygen
Organism that can respire with or without oxygen
Muscle fibres adapted for aerobic respiration
Muscle fibres adapted for anaerobic respiration
Aerobic: uses O₂, produces CO₂ + H₂O, ~36-38 ATP
Anaerobic: no O₂, produces lactic acid (animals) or ethanol + CO₂ (yeast), ~2 ATP
Aerobic is more efficient but needs oxygen
Anaerobic is faster but less efficient
Both types used during exercise depending on intensity
Different muscle fibres specialised for each type
Different organisms may be obligate or facultative anaerobes
